Teachers often ask "Which assistant is easier to use?" This page brings the problem down to the same thing: using the public paper of Walters and Wilder (2023), write a page of Chinese material description. First, show the papers and report value tables that have been checked for the course, and then explain what is required for each of the three entrances. The paper studied specific models and tasks at the time; 55% and 18% are error rates that cannot be generalized to today's products. The three routes are selected examples for course writing and have not yet been executed on Claude, ChatGPT or DeepSeek respectively, and there are no three-party performance, speed or cost comparisons.
Claude route: The official document description supports executing code, processing uploaded materials, and generating Word and other files. If the current account has opened the file tool, you can directly provide the paper PDF, and let it first list the original text positioning, denominator and restrictions, and then organize it into a description draft. If the table cannot be read, a manually checked excerpt will be used instead, and no guessing is allowed. ChatGPT route: This specifically refers to the file processing capabilities in ChatGPT Work and official instructions; provide papers and report value tables together, require editable diagrams and explanation files, check the numbers and graphics in the preview, and then download the file. Whether the common chat portal has the same tool needs to be checked on site. DeepSeek route: This specifically refers to the course web plan that connects to the DeepSeek API; verified text and values ​​are provided, and the model is drafted and exported by the application's file tool. API response, web page retrieval, calculation, and Word export each have their own tools and records. You cannot say that the entire process is complete just by looking at a single answer. The official API also announced the Search/Fetch and Agent integration portal. This page does not describe DeepSeek as naturally unable to connect to the Internet or generate files. Let’s jointly check an error-prone area: 55% and 18% correspond to the fictitious proportion of all references; 43% and 24% correspond to the substantial error proportion in real references. The two sets have different denominators and cannot be combined into an "overall error rate". Tables 3 and 4 of the original text and the description of counting in the text should be read together. If you need to determine whether the new documents are authentic item by item, you can also use academic search, DOI and original text review; this is not something that can be accomplished with three assistants voting for each other. Elicit and Consensus are portals for discovery and organization of research, and Connected Papers are used to explore document relationships. For their coverage and full-text availability, please check the official instructions in Section 5. After this page is changed to a branded example, the division of labor of these professional tools is still retained.

pairs: 01 Scientific Research AI: Capabilities, Principles and Academic Boundaries
After AI generates explanations or predictions, it must be clear: which judgment is supported by the research.
Use existing features to estimate unknown results.
For example, predicting properties based on material composition.
Need to check the test set, error and applicable range.
Describe the mechanism through which the phenomenon may occur.
Requires evidence of theory, measurement, and supporting mechanisms.
A reasonable story is not enough to establish the mechanism.
Determine whether changing a factor will change the result.
An appropriate research design and identification of hypotheses are required.
Accurate correlations or predictions cannot alone prove cause and effect.
For example: AI discovers that "a certain feature and result change at the same time", which can form clues to be tested.
To write "Changing this feature leads to a change in the result", it is necessary to check for confounding, chronological order and other explanations.
Model output should retain the strength of conclusions that the research design can support. Mechanism schematics and natural language reasoning also require evidence.
items.note:
This page talks about the levels of scientific research inference. The examples are method descriptions and do not make up specific experiments or numerical values. Prediction can be used to screen candidate materials without automatically establishing mechanisms and causal conclusions; causal judgment does not rely solely on random experiments. Specific research can include quasi-experiments, observational identification and corresponding hypotheses. A mechanism is not considered proven just because a model generates a detailed explanation. Details of technical methods are developed in the research design and data analysis chapters.

items.note:
This page compares three publishers by use. Nature's current webpage lists extensive writing support as a use that requires careful handling, requiring manual supervision, verification, and disclosure; it cannot be concluded that all language editors are exempt from claims. The first page of Science's official rules distinguishes between improving clarity, drafting or translating the text, modifying code functions, and research analysis: the former does not require a statement, drafting and translation indicate the model and version in the acknowledgments, and the latter two categories are in the method description. If you only change the code format and do not change the function, you can avoid the declaration. Schematic illustrations are not allowed in principle, exceptions must be discussed with the editor. Pages 1-2 also limit the input of review and rework materials. Please see the supporting instructions for details. PLOS FAQ exempts the disclosure of pure language improvements and recommends disclosure of translations; schematic diagrams can be used, but they must be disclosed and verified in the figure captions and do not pretend to be original data. None of the three transfer author responsibility to the tool. This round actually reads the web page and views the two-page original PDF of Science; the PDF metadata creation date is 2026-09-01, and the effective date of the independent policy is not marked in the text.

pairs: 01 Scientific Research AI: Capabilities, Principles and Academic Boundaries
Four conditions for scientific research credibility
AI-assisted results need to be checked by evidence and methods before they are included in papers, applications or reports.
Papers, data and guides have locatable originals.
If there is a title or DOI, the actual corresponding content still needs to be confirmed.
Keep records of input, methods, code, and processing.
The calculation can be reproduced, the modification has a basis, and the versions can be distinguished.
The conclusion is consistent with the research objects, conditions and design.
Do not write speculations as results, and do not write correlations directly as causation.
The researcher checks the content and discloses it for use as required.
Language revised to preserve facts, figures, citations, and limitations.
The subsequent chapters are based on this: literature, data, charts, papers and application materials, each has evidence that needs to be checked.
Source: NIST AI 600-1 (2024); Walters & Wilder (2023), Tables 3, 4; Nature Portfolio AI policy; PLOS AI policy
items.note:
This page is the usage framework of the course based on the aforementioned principles, empirical research and publication standards. There is no requirement for classroom exercises, operation check-ins or for students to submit documents. Authentic sources do not guarantee that the conclusions are valid, and reproducibility does not guarantee that the methods are reasonable. The four items need to be judged based on specific research. The subsequent Humanizer chapter will show how to improve the language without changing the strength of evidence and usage facts; the Agent and Harness chapters will explain how to save execution status, sources and files.

First separate the four levels. Do not let students remember that Agentic AI is equal to ChatGPT, and AI Agent is equal to Codex. Agentic can modify the working method or system characteristics; Agent usually refers to the system responsible for performing tasks. Definitions in academia and industry are not entirely consistent and a working definition adopted by the course is provided here. Product capabilities will change, and this lesson does not describe interface differences as permanent boundaries.
Detailed teaching content:
Model: Generates judgment, text, or tool call requests based on input. : The model itself is not equivalent to a system that completes file tasks.
AI Agent: An execution system that combines tools and feedback to advance tasks around goals. : Specific systems vary in their degree of autonomy, authority, and reliability.
Agentic AI: Describes the way AI works with characteristics such as goal orientation and multi-step actions. : The usage of terminology has not yet been unified, and this course explains it based on behavior.
ChatGPT / Codex: Products and work environments people use. : They can support multiple collaboration methods and have overlapping capabilities.
